note: Synthetic demonstration data for the Point32Health Agentic Incident Workbench POC. Not real Point32Health incidents, systems, members, providers or employees. No PHI or PII.

incidents.title: Payment API returning HTTP 504 after idle period
incidents.description: Production Payment API is intermittently returning HTTP 504 Gateway Timeout on the first request after an idle period. The issue appears after the container app scales from zero to one replica. Subsequent requests succeed once the application is warm. Initial investigation suggests application startup may take longer than the API gateway (APIM) timeout.
incidents.business_impact: Payment calls after quiet periods fail with HTTP 504 and must be retried; Finance and provider remittance see intermittent failures.
incidents.complexity: Single round: documented ITOPS demo scenario

logs.text: HTTP 504 on POST /payments: backend did not respond within 30 s; occurs only on the first request after 15+ minutes without traffic.
Replica scaled 0 -> 1 at the time of each failing request; container ready after 38-44 s (image pull, runtime start, dependency warm-up).
Requests after the replica is warm complete in about 180 ms; no 504s while traffic is continuous.

metrics.name: HTTP 504 rate on first request after idle

changes.title: Payment API scale-to-zero enabled (cost optimisation)
changes.detail: Container app minimum replicas lowered from 1 to 0 for the production revision.

history.title: Reporting API 504 after idle on scale-to-zero revision
history.resolution: Minimum replicas set to 1; gateway timeout raised.

kb.title: Payment API cold-start HTTP 504 remediation
kb.summary: Keep min replicas at 1 for production APIs and set the APIM backend timeout above the worst-case cold-start time.

hypotheses.title: Cold start after scale-to-zero exceeds the 30 s gateway timeout
hypotheses.why: 504s occur only on the first request after idle, exactly when the replica scales from 0 to 1 and takes 38-44 s to become ready.

hypotheses.title: Payments database slow to accept new connections
hypotheses.why: A slow dependency could delay the first request.

hypotheses.title: Intermittent network loss between APIM and the container app
hypotheses.why: Gateway timeouts can come from network drops.

critic: Directly supported: the 504 timing matches every scale-up from zero.
Warm requests succeed in 180 ms, so the database is not the bottleneck.
Failures only after idle periods do not fit random network loss.
script.root_cause: Change CHG-DEMO-7301 set the Payment API container app to scale to zero; the first request after an idle period triggers a cold start of 38-44 seconds, which exceeds the 30 second APIM backend timeout, so the gateway returns HTTP 504 before the replica is ready.
contributing: The APIM timeout was not reviewed when scale-to-zero was enabled.
No synthetic check calls the API after idle periods.

remediation.step: Record the current min/max replica settings and the APIM backend timeout in the incident.
remediation.expected: Settings captured: min replicas 0, APIM timeout 30 s.

remediation.step: Set min replicas to 1 for the production revision (standard change template 'Scale settings').
Raise the APIM backend timeout for the Payment API from 30 s to 60 s.
remediation.expected: Gateway timeout exceeds the worst-case cold start.

remediation.step: Let the service idle for 15 minutes, then send a test payment request.
remediation.expected: HTTP 200 on the first request after idle.

script.rollback: Restore the previous scale settings and APIM timeout from the recorded values.
prevention: Keep a minimum replica of 1 for latency-sensitive production APIs.
Alert when startup time approaches the gateway timeout; add a synthetic check after idle periods.

incidents.title: Claims adjudication service intermittently returning HTTP 504 during peak processing
incidents.description: Since about 09:10 ET the claims adjudication service returns intermittent HTTP 504 Gateway Timeout responses to the claims workbench. Roughly 1 in 6 adjudication requests fail and examiners have to resubmit. It is worst between 09:00 and 11:00 when volume peaks. Nothing was reported yesterday.
incidents.business_impact: Claims examiners lose time resubmitting; adjudication throughput down about 15% during the morning peak.
incidents.complexity: Multi-agent: needs a second evidence round

logs.text: 504 on POST /adjudicate after 30.0 s upstream timeout; 212 of 1,290 requests in the last 30 min.
Request processing time spikes to 28-31 s; no exceptions logged at ERROR level.

changes.title: claims-adjudication-api config release 24.11.2
changes.detail: Tuned datasource settings and logging levels.

history.title: Claims adjudication slow after pricing engine patch
history.resolution: Pricing engine cache warmed; latency recovered.

kb.title: Claims adjudication API: diagnosing gateway timeouts
kb.summary: Check upstream latency, DB pool saturation and pricing engine response time before restarting pods.

deep.text: HikariPool-1 - Connection is not available, request timed out after 30000ms (total=40, active=40, idle=0, waiting=57).
pricing-engine p95 latency 180 ms, unchanged from baseline.
datasource.maximumPoolSize changed from 100 to 40.

hypotheses.title: Database connection pool exhaustion in claims-adjudication-api
hypotheses.why: Requests stall for ~30 s, matching a pool wait timeout; a datasource change shipped yesterday.

hypotheses.title: Slow pricing-engine dependency
hypotheses.why: A previous incident had the same symptom after a pricing engine patch.

hypotheses.title: API gateway timeout set too low
hypotheses.why: Failures happen exactly at the 30 s gateway timeout.

critic: Plausible, but no pool metrics yet; the change ticket only says 'tuned datasource settings'. Need pool saturation evidence.
No pricing-engine latency data was gathered; history alone is weak.
Raising the gateway timeout would hide the symptom; it doesn't explain why requests take 30 s.
script.root_cause: Config release CHG-DEMO-3101 lowered the claims-adjudication-api database pool from 100 to 40 connections; at peak volume all 40 are busy, requests wait the full 30 s pool timeout and the gateway returns 504.
contributing: The pool size change was bundled with logging changes and not load tested.
No alert on connection-pool saturation.

remediation.step: Confirm pool saturation on the pool dashboard (active = max, waiting > 0).
remediation.expected: Saturation confirmed during the failure window.

remediation.step: Restore datasource.maximumPoolSize to 100 through the approved config pipeline.
remediation.expected: New config version deployed to all pods.

remediation.step: Rolling restart of claims-adjudication-api pods, one at a time.
remediation.expected: All pods healthy; no request errors during the rollout.

remediation.step: Watch gateway 5xx rate for 15 minutes.

script.rollback: Re-apply config version 24.11.2 and restart pods if DB CPU exceeds 80% after the change.
prevention: Alert when pool waiting > 0 for 5 minutes.
Load test datasource changes before release.

exec_fail.error: Config pipeline returned HTTP 503 (deployment agent busy). No change applied.

incidents.title: Nightly claims adjudication batch delayed; backlog of pending claims growing
incidents.description: The nightly auto-adjudication batch, normally finished by 05:30 ET, was still running at 08:00. About 41,000 claims are still pending and the backlog is growing as new claims arrive. Downstream payment file cut-off is 12:00.
incidents.business_impact: Risk of missing the 12:00 payment file cut-off; provider payments could slip by a day.
incidents.complexity: Straightforward investigation; verification needs a second pass

logs.text: Job CLM-AUTOADJ started 01:00; step 3 (adjudicate) throughput 140 claims/min vs normal 900.
Sessions from CLM-AUTOADJ waiting on lock: relation claim_header (RowExclusiveLock) blocked by pid 48812.
pid 48812: month-end claims aging report, started 00:55, running SELECT ... FOR UPDATE on claim_header.

changes.title: Month-end reporting schedule update
changes.detail: Claims aging report moved from 22:00 to 00:55.

kb.title: Claims batch window and reporting blackout
kb.summary: No locking reports on claim tables between 01:00 and 05:30.

hypotheses.title: Lock contention from the rescheduled month-end aging report
hypotheses.why: Batch sessions wait on a lock held by the report, which was moved into the batch window.

hypotheses.title: Not enough batch workers
Upstream claims intake file arrived late
hypotheses.why: A late file would delay the start.

critic: Strongly supported: lock chain and the schedule change line up.
Worker count is unchanged; low throughput is explained by lock waits.
The job started on time at 01:00, so a late file is contradicted.
script.root_cause: CHG-DEMO-3088 moved the month-end claims aging report to 00:55; its SELECT ... FOR UPDATE on claim_header blocks the 01:00 auto-adjudication batch, cutting throughput from 900 to 140 claims per minute.
contributing: The reporting change did not check the batch blackout window in KB-DEMO-1188.
Batch has no alert for lock waits.

remediation.step: Get approval from the report owner to cancel the running aging report (pid 48812).
Cancel the report session with pg_cancel_backend (not terminate).
Monitor batch throughput for 10 minutes.
Reschedule the aging report to 22:00 via a change request.
remediation.expected: Change raised for the schedule fix.

script.rollback: No rollback needed for cancelling a read report; rerun the report after the batch completes.
prevention: Add the batch window to the reporting change checklist.
Alert on lock waits > 5 min for batch sessions.

followup.step: Temporarily raise CLM-AUTOADJ parallelism from 4 to 8 workers until the backlog is below 5,000, then restore 4.

incidents.title: Duplicate claim records created between claims intake and adjudication
incidents.description: Claims examiners found duplicate claim records for the same claim control number in the adjudication queue since yesterday afternoon. About 2% of electronically received claims appear twice. Duplicates risk double payment if not caught.
incidents.business_impact: Potential duplicate payments; QA team manually reviewing ~600 claims per day.
incidents.complexity: Multi-agent: needs a second evidence round

logs.text: WARN processing time 48 s for message batch; consumer lock lost, message abandoned.
1,214 claim control numbers with 2 records since 14:00 yesterday.

changes.title: Intake consumer performance tuning
changes.detail: Message lock duration reduced from 120 s to 30 s.

kb.title: Claims intake message handling
kb.summary: Consumers must use the claim control number as the idempotency key.

deep.text: Message 7f3a... delivered twice (deliveryCount=2) after lock expiry at 30 s; both deliveries committed.
Idempotency check on claim control number is skipped when the claim source is EDI (feature flag edi_idempotency=false since 2025).

hypotheses.title: Messages redelivered after shorter lock duration and processed twice
hypotheses.why: Lock duration cut to 30 s while processing takes up to 48 s.

hypotheses.title: Submitters sending the same claim twice
hypotheses.why: Duplicates share a claim control number.

hypotheses.title: Database replication creating duplicate rows
hypotheses.why: Duplicates appear in the adjudication queue.

critic: Redelivery explains duplicates only if idempotency is not enforced; KB says it should be. Need delivery counts and the idempotency path.
Submitter resends would carry different interchange numbers; not checked yet.
No replication errors reported; unsupported.
script.root_cause: CHG-DEMO-3092 cut the intake consumer's message lock from 120 s to 30 s; batches taking up to 48 s lose the lock and are redelivered, and because the claim-control-number idempotency check is disabled for EDI claims both deliveries are committed.
contributing: Feature flag edi_idempotency has been off since an earlier migration.
No duplicate-claim monitor before adjudication.

remediation.step: Restore message lock duration to 120 s via config pipeline.
Enable edi_idempotency in a staged rollout (10%, then 100%).
Run the read-only duplicate report for the affected window and hand the list to Claims QA.
Claims QA voids duplicates through the claims correction workflow after business sign-off.

script.rollback: Disable edi_idempotency if valid claims are rejected; lock duration change can be reverted independently.
prevention: Duplicate claim monitor before adjudication.
Test lock duration against p99 processing time.

incidents.title: Claims processing API response times elevated since release
incidents.description: Claim lookup and line-detail calls from the claims workbench take 6-9 seconds instead of under 1 second since Sunday's release. No errors, just slow. All examiners affected.
incidents.business_impact: Examiner productivity down ~20%; no data impact.
incidents.complexity: Straightforward

logs.text: GET /claims/{id}/lines: 7.2 s, of which 7.0 s in query claim_line WHERE member_ref = ?
Seq Scan on claim_line (rows=38M) for member_ref predicate; previously Index Scan.

changes.title: Claims release 24.11 schema migration
changes.detail: Renamed claim_line.member_id to member_ref.

kb.title: Schema migration checklist
kb.summary: Recreate dependent indexes when renaming indexed columns.

hypotheses.title: Index lost during the column rename in release 24.11
hypotheses.why: Query plan changed from index scan to sequential scan on the renamed column.

hypotheses.title: Database under-provisioned for current volume
Network latency between API and database

critic: Well supported by the plan change.
No CPU or IO saturation evidence.
The trace shows time spent in the query, not the network.
script.root_cause: Release 24.11 migration CHG-DEMO-3075 renamed claim_line.member_id to member_ref with a drop-and-add that did not recreate the index, so line-detail queries do a sequential scan of 38 million rows.
contributing: Migration checklist step to recreate indexes was skipped.
No query-plan regression test in the release pipeline.

remediation.step: Create index CONCURRENTLY on claim_line(member_ref) during business hours (non-blocking).
ANALYZE claim_line.
Confirm the query plan uses the new index.
Monitor line-detail p95 latency for 15 minutes.

script.rollback: DROP INDEX CONCURRENTLY if write latency on claim_line degrades by more than 20%.
prevention: Add a plan-regression test for top 20 queries.
Enforce the index step in the migration checklist.

incidents.title: Claims status updates not reflected consistently across internal applications
incidents.description: Claims adjudicated this morning show 'Pended' in the customer service desktop but 'Paid' in the claims workbench. Customer service reps are giving members wrong status information.
incidents.business_impact: Wrong status given to members; repeat calls to the contact center.
incidents.complexity: Multi-agent: needs a second evidence round

logs.text: Cache HIT for claim status keys 97% of requests (normally ~60%).
Processed ClaimStatusChanged events normally; lag 2 s.

changes.title: claims-status-api cache configuration
changes.detail: Cache settings consolidated into shared config file.

history.title: Status lag due to event consumer backlog

kb.title: Claims status cache design
kb.summary: Status cache entries have a 5-minute TTL and are invalidated on ClaimStatusChanged.

deep.text: statusCache.ttlSeconds 300 -> 86400; statusCache.invalidateOnEvent key missing in consolidated file (defaults to false).
Key claim:status:C-…  TTL 79,412 s; value 'PENDED' while claims-db shows 'PAID'.

hypotheses.title: Status cache serving stale entries after config consolidation
hypotheses.why: Cache hit ratio jumped to 97% after the cache config change.

hypotheses.title: Status event consumer lagging
hypotheses.why: A previous incident had the same symptom.

hypotheses.title: Customer service desktop reading a different data source
hypotheses.why: Only one app shows the wrong value.

critic: High hit ratio suggests staleness but doesn't prove it; need TTL and invalidation settings.
Contradicted: consumer lag is 2 s.
The desktop reads claims-status-api, same as other apps; unsupported.
script.root_cause: CHG-DEMO-3097 consolidated cache settings, raising the status cache TTL from 5 minutes to 24 hours and dropping invalidateOnEvent, so claims-status-api keeps serving the pre-adjudication status for up to a day.
contributing: Config consolidation had no diff review for default values.
No staleness check between cache and claims-db.

remediation.step: Restore ttlSeconds=300 and invalidateOnEvent=true via config pipeline.
Flush claim:status:* keys in the status cache.
Sample 200 claims and compare cache vs claims-db status.
Notify Member Services that status is accurate again.
remediation.expected: Notice sent to contact center leads.

script.rollback: Revert to previous config version; flushing the cache is safe and self-healing.
prevention: Schema-validate cache config with required keys.
Hourly staleness sampling alert.

exec_fail.error: Cache flush command timed out (Redis replica failover in progress). No keys flushed.

incidents.title: Member portal login intermittently failing
incidents.description: Members report the portal login sometimes fails with 'Something went wrong, please try again', then works on a second or third attempt. Contact center call volume about login is up 3x today.
incidents.business_impact: Members cannot reliably sign in; contact center volume up 3x for login issues.
incidents.complexity: Multi-agent: needs a second evidence round

logs.text: Token validation failed: IDX10501/iat in the future for ~33% of sign-ins.
Traffic evenly split across 3 web nodes (web-01, web-02, web-03).

changes.title: Monthly OS patching: member portal web tier
changes.detail: Applied OS image 2026.11 to web-01..03.

history.title: Portal login failures after IdP certificate renewal

kb.title: Portal sign-in troubleshooting
kb.summary: Check IdP metadata, token lifetimes and node clock sync.

deep.text: 100% of token failures on web-02; 0% on web-01 and web-03.
Clock offset -94 s; time sync service stopped since patch reboot.

hypotheses.title: One web node has clock skew, rejecting fresh tokens
hypotheses.why: 'iat in the future' errors appear on about a third of sign-ins, matching one of three nodes.

hypotheses.title: Identity provider certificate or metadata mismatch
hypotheses.why: Previous login incident had this cause.

hypotheses.title: Patching broke a shared library on all nodes

critic: The 1-in-3 pattern is suggestive but not proven per node; need a per-node breakdown and clock data.
A metadata mismatch would fail every sign-in, not a third.
A broken library would affect all nodes equally; contradicted by the intermittency.
script.root_cause: After the CHG-DEMO-2210 patch reboot, the time sync service on web-02 did not restart; its clock drifted 94 seconds behind, so it rejects freshly issued tokens as 'issued in the future', failing about one third of sign-ins.
contributing: Patch runbook has no post-reboot time sync check.
No per-node error alerting.

remediation.step: Drain web-02 from the load balancer.
Start and enable the time sync service on web-02; confirm offset < 1 s.
Return web-02 to the pool.
Monitor login failure rate for 15 minutes.

script.rollback: Keep web-02 drained if the offset does not converge; two nodes carry normal load.
prevention: Add time sync verification to the patch runbook.
Alert on node clock offset > 5 s.

incidents.title: Member eligibility information not loading after successful sign-in
incidents.description: Members can sign in to the portal, but the 'My coverage' panel shows 'Coverage information is unavailable' for everyone since about 07:00 ET. Claims and ID card pages work.
incidents.business_impact: Members cannot see coverage; calls to the contact center about eligibility increasing.

logs.text: TLS handshake failed calling eligibility-api: certificate expired (client certificate CN=member-coverage-bff, notAfter 2026-11-11T07:00Z).
mTLS rejects from client member-coverage-bff: 100% since 07:00.

history.title: Provider portal outage from expired client certificate

kb.title: Rotating mTLS client certificates
kb.summary: Issue from internal CA, store in secret store, reload BFF pods.

hypotheses.title: Expired mTLS client certificate between coverage BFF and eligibility API
hypotheses.why: Handshake failures cite certificate expiry at exactly 07:00.

hypotheses.title: Eligibility API outage
Portal session issue

critic: Directly evidenced.
Other eligibility clients are healthy; only this client is rejected.
Other pages work in the same session; contradicted.
script.root_cause: The member-coverage-bff mTLS client certificate expired at 07:00Z and was not on auto-renewal, so the eligibility API rejects every call and the coverage panel shows no data.
contributing: Certificate was issued manually and not tracked for renewal.
No certificate-expiry alert for this client.

remediation.step: Issue a new client certificate from the internal CA for CN=member-coverage-bff.
Store the certificate in the secret store under the existing secret name.
Rolling restart of member-coverage-bff pods to load the new certificate.
Check coverage panel error rate.

prevention: Enroll the certificate in automated renewal.
Alert 30 days before any client certificate expires.

incidents.title: Digital claims submission returning an unexpected application error
incidents.description: Members submitting a reimbursement claim with attachments in the portal get 'An unexpected error occurred' on the final step. Submissions without attachments go through. Started yesterday evening.
incidents.business_impact: Members cannot submit reimbursement claims with receipts; paper claims increasing.
incidents.complexity: Multi-agent: needs a second evidence round

logs.text: POST /claims/submit failed; response body not JSON; generic error displayed.
No requests logged for failed submissions.

changes.title: Web application firewall policy update
changes.detail: Hardened request inspection rules for public endpoints.

kb.title: Member claim attachments
kb.summary: Attachments up to 10 MB per file are supported.

deep.text: Blocked: request body size 3.4 MB exceeds limit 1 MB (rule MaxBodySize) - HTTP 413.
maxRequestBodyKb 12288 -> 1024 for /claims/*.

hypotheses.title: Requests blocked before reaching the API by the updated WAF policy
hypotheses.why: API logs show no requests for failed submissions; WAF changed yesterday.

hypotheses.title: Document store rejecting attachments
Frontend bug in the final step

critic: Likely, but which rule blocks it and why only attachments? Need WAF block logs.
If the document store rejected files, the API would log the call; it logs nothing.
Submissions without attachments use the same final step and work.
script.root_cause: WAF policy update CHG-DEMO-2231 lowered the maximum request body for /claims/* from 12 MB to 1 MB, so submissions with receipts over 1 MB are blocked with HTTP 413 before reaching the API and the portal shows a generic error.
contributing: The portal does not map 413 to a helpful message.
WAF change was not tested with attachment flows.

remediation.step: Raise maxRequestBodyKb for /claims/* back to 12288 through a WAF policy change.
Submit a test claim with a 5 MB synthetic attachment in the test member account.
Monitor submission failure rate for 30 minutes.
Raise a story to show a size-limit message on 413.

script.rollback: Re-apply the previous WAF policy version.
prevention: Include attachment upload in WAF change test plan.
Alert on WAF block spikes per route.

incidents.title: Member portal showing outdated claims status
incidents.description: Members see claims as 'In process' in the portal hours after they were paid. Internal systems show the right status. Started this morning.
incidents.business_impact: Members call to ask about paid claims; status confusion.
incidents.complexity: Straightforward

logs.text: GET /api/member/claims: cache status HIT, age 14,200 s.
Responses sent with Cache-Control: private, no-store.

changes.title: CDN performance rules for member portal
changes.detail: Added caching rule for /api/member/* static-like responses.

kb.title: Member portal caching rules
kb.summary: Member-specific API responses must never be cached at the CDN.

hypotheses.title: New CDN rule caching member claims API responses
hypotheses.why: CDN reports cache HITs with age of ~4 hours for a no-store API.

hypotheses.title: Claims status service cache stale
hypotheses.why: Similar symptom in internal apps before.

hypotheses.title: Browser caching

critic: Supported; also a privacy concern since responses are member-specific.
Internal systems are correct; contradicted.
API sends no-store; CDN age proves server-side caching.

Purge CDN cache for /api/member/*.
Check CDN cache status for claims-view calls.

prevention: CDN rule linting: block caching on authenticated API paths.
Synthetic check comparing portal vs internal status.

incidents.title: Provider directory search returning incomplete provider information

hypotheses.title: Source provider data incomplete

incidents.title: Eligibility verification API intermittently failing
incidents.description: Provider office staff checking eligibility through the provider portal get intermittent 'Unable to verify eligibility' errors, about 8% of checks since Monday.
incidents.business_impact: Provider offices delay appointments or call the provider service line.
incidents.complexity: Straightforward; remediation needs manual takeover

logs.text: Upstream rules engine returned HTTP 429 Too Many Requests; request failed without retry.
Rate limit 200 req/s per client; eligibility-verify-api peaking at 240 req/s since Monday.

changes.title: New clearinghouse partner onboarded to eligibility API
changes.detail: Partner real-time eligibility traffic routed to eligibility-verify-api.

kb.title: Rules engine quotas
kb.summary: Quota increases go through the rules engine platform team; clients must back off on 429.

hypotheses.title: Rules engine rate limit exceeded after new partner traffic
hypotheses.why: 429 responses; traffic above the 200 req/s quota since the partner went live.

hypotheses.title: Rules engine capacity problem
Bad member data for some checks

critic: Well supported.

Failures are spread across members; no data pattern.
script.root_cause: Traffic from the clearinghouse partner onboarded in CHG-DEMO-4020 pushed eligibility-verify-api above its 200 req/s rules engine quota; excess calls get HTTP 429 and the API fails them without retry.

asset_policy.rule: Hardware fault on a device under warranty: vendor repair under warranty, no cost to the department.
Replace when the device is older than 4 years, or when an out-of-warranty (or unknown-warranty) repair would cost more than 50% of the standard replacement ($1,100 Standard Laptop).

requests.title: How much parental leave can I take, and how do I apply?
requests.description: My partner and I are expecting a baby in March. How much paid parental leave can I take, can I split it, and how do I apply? I've been here three years.

script.answer: With three years of service you're eligible for 12 weeks of paid parental leave. You can take it in one block or in blocks of at least 2 weeks within 12 months of the birth. Tell your manager at least 30 days before you start and submit the leave request in the HR portal; HR confirms within 5 business days.
conditions: Tell your manager at least 30 days before leave starts
Use within 12 months of the birth
tasks: Tell your manager the planned leave dates

requests.title: Add my spouse to my medical plan after getting married
requests.description: I got married on 1 November and want to add my spouse to my medical and dental cover. What do I need to do and when does cover start?

dates: 1 Dec 2026: last day to request the change
script.answer: Marriage is a qualifying life event, so you can add your spouse to medical and dental cover within 30 days, by 1 December. Upload your marriage certificate with the change request. Cover for your spouse starts on the first of the month after HR approves the change.
tasks: Submit the benefits change with the marriage certificate
Confirm the cover start date to the employee
